content: 1. Rilpivirine levels may be increased due to its interaction with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required in this context. 2. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 3. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that carry a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be done cautiously. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ziprasidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 5. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 6. Crizotinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 7. Co-administration of rilpivirine with adagrasib should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 8. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 9. Alfuzosin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours afterward. 11. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of amiodarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 12. Co-administration of rilpivirine with amisulpride should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. 13. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of amitriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of amoxapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 15. Co-administration of rilpivirine with anagrelide should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 16. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of apomorphine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 17. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 18. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 19. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of arsenic trioxide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 20. Co-administration of rilpivirine with artemether should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 21. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of artemether/lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 22. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 23. Asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 24. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 25. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 26. Co-administration of rilpivirine with atidarsagene autotemcel should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should not be taken for at least 1 month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 27. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 28. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 29. Co-administration of rilpivirine with bedaquiline should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 30. Co-administration of rilpivirine with betibeglogene autotemcel should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. ARTs should not be taken for at least 1 month before mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 31. Co-administration of rilpivirine with buprenorphine (in various formulations) should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 32. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 34. Calcium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 35. Calcium citrate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 36. Calcium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 37. Calcium/vitamin D decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 38. Co-administration of rilpivirine with carbamazepine is contraindicated. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may result in a loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 39. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 40. Chlorpromazine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 41. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 42. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 43. Citalopram increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 44. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Rilpivirine also increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. 45. Clomipramine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 46. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 47. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 48. Crizotinib increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, but the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Cyclobenzaprine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 50. Dasatinib increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 51. Degarelix increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 52. Co-administration of rilpivirine with desflurane should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 53. Desipramine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes should be approached with caution. 54. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances, such as bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, may increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes or sudden death. 55. Co-administration of rilpivirine with dexamethasone is contraindicated. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This may result in a loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 56. Co-administration of rilpivirine with dexlansoprazole is contraindicated. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Concurrent use may cause treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. 57. Didanosine and rilpivirine interact by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach and at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine.
